newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Trostberg shares dip on results.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Trostberg shares dip on results.

text.p: Shares in German specialty chemicals group SKW Trostberg dropped sharply on Friday after nine-month results sparked investor worries that its full year figures may fall short of optimistic forecasts.
The group's majority shareholder, VIAG AG, said sales rose four percent to 2.97 billion marks ($1.97 billion) while operating results were mostly unchanged in the nine months to September 30.

SKW Trostberg spokesman Rainer Lihotzky declined to comment on the numbers, saying only that the group was sticking by its forecasts for higher profits. The results will be officially announced at a news conference on November 20.
VIAG, previewing the SKW Trostberg numbers as part of its own nine-month results announcement, said strong growth in the chemicals and construction chemical divisions boosted results.

SKW Trostberg, the world's leading construction chemicals group since its takeover of Master Builder Technologies (MTB) from Swiss group Sandoz AG this year, predicted full year pre-tax earnings would jump by about 30 percent.

The information unnerved investors enough to send shares down nine percent in early Frankfurt dealings. Shares later pared some losses but remained down over three percent at 43.50 marks in late afternoon trade.
BHF Bank analyst Ronald Koehler said the numbers indicated some weakness and prompted him to downgrade his share recommendation to hold from buy and cut earnings estimates.
Koehler said he had cut his 1996 earnings per share estimate to 2.25 marks per share from 2.65.
"We will still see growth at the company but it just won't be as strong," he said.
Other analysts stopped short of making changes to their forecasts, however, saying they needed more detailed information from the group.
SKW Trostberg floated its shares in spring 1995 and generally delighted investors with promises of ongoing strong earnings growth, powered partly by more acquisitions.
Since June 1995 the share value has jumped 55 percent.
The group's first half profits jumped 62 percent to 131 million marks, while sales rose 12 percent to 2.1 billion marks.

At that time investors were relieved SKW Trostberg was not planning to raise capital to finance the 1.3 billion Swiss francs ($1.02 billion) takeover price for MBT. But sources close to the company said the group may still decide to issue new shares next year.
